overview: Ancient India from the Indus to the Guptas: 43 official Group 1 questions (2008-2024), heaviest on Vedic Age (8), Mauryas (6), Satavahanas (6) and Indus sites (5). 27 are one-liners (who/where/which text); since 2023 APPSC adds statement-based, matching and 'which of these belong to period X' multiple-correct items (about 9 per paper).

possibility.angle: Indus sites and their signature finds
possibility.what_they_ask: which site had beads/scale/rice/dock; main foreign contact (Mesopotamia); late Harappan features
function of seals and sealings; natural targets: Pasupati seal, mother goddess, Great Bath

possibility.angle: Vedic texts, society, religion and pottery
possibility.what_they_ask: which text first mentions X (varna, moneylending); Rig Vedic gods' roles; marriage forms; philosophy school-theory; Later Vedic pottery
Mahajanapada-capital matching; Nanda canal in Hathigumpha
founder's varna; Jain languages; Buddha's life places; who propounded which doctrine
titles (Devanampiya); scripts and content of Asokan edicts; Mauryan monuments; Arthashastra officials
Greek river names; Central Asian items introduced (dress, cavalry)

possibility.evidence: 6 Qs: 2010×2, 2012, 2019, 2023, 2024; also many related APPSC AP History items
possibility.what_they_ask: inscription-issuer pairs (Nasik, Nanaghat); court authors (Hala, Gunadhya, Sarvavarman, Kutuhala); terms like kataka; Buddhist sites
which texts record the Yavana invasion under Pushyamitra
who started the Gupta era; ruler sequence; who defeated the Sakas; guild features; founder of Nalanda

traps.trap: [Name clash] Same-name ruler from another dynasty
traps.spot: Options carry Chandragupta I / Chandragupta Maurya / Chandragupta II
traps.fix: Tie the event to the dynasty first: abdication+Jain = Maurya; Gupta era = Chandragupta I; Sakas = Chandragupta II
traps.pyq: 'During the reign of Chandragupta-I, the Sakas were defeated' → it was Chandragupta II [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#8]; abdication → Chandragupta Maurya [group1-prelims-2010#7]

traps.trap: Inscription paired with the wrong issuer
traps.spot: Wrong-pair list of inscriptions with famous rulers
traps.fix: Nanaghat = Naganika; Nasik = Gautami Balasri; Junagadh = Rudradaman; Hathigumpha = Kharavela

traps.trap: Author swapped among the Satavahana-age writers
traps.spot: Matching books with Nagarjuna, Kundakunda, Sarvavarman, Kutuhala
traps.fix: Katantra = Sarvavarman; Lilavai = Kutuhala; Samayasara = Kundakunda (Jain); Prajnaparamita = Nagarjuna (Mahayana)

traps.trap: Later item slipped into a period list
traps.spot: 'Which belong to the Later Vedic / Sunga period' with one item from a later age
traps.fix: Check the date of each item: NBPW c.600-200 BC (not Later Vedic); Mudrarakshasa is about Chandragupta Maurya
traps.pyq: NBPW excluded from Later Vedic pottery [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#2]; Mudrarakshasa not a Sunga source [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#8]

traps.trap: Plausible but non-existent content in an edict
traps.spot: A statement credits an Asokan edict with an event known only from chronicles
traps.fix: Succession war is in Dipavamsa/Mahavamsa, not in any edict; RE XIII = Kalinga + five Greek kings
traps.pyq: 'IV and V edicts mentioned the war of succession' → false [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#5]

traps.spot: Rig Vedic god statement that sounds right ('mother of all gods')
traps.fix: Aditi is mother of the Adityas; Prithvi is earth; Agni the messenger; Dyaus = sky father
traps.pyq: 'Prithvi was the mother of all Gods' → Aditi [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#2]

traps.trap: Absolute negative on a true practice
traps.spot: 'They never used X' about a language or practice
traps.fix: Check the fact, not the word: Jains did write important works in Apabhramsa

traps.spot: 'Which was not a feature of Gupta guilds'
traps.fix: Gupta guilds were autonomous: own seals, militia, banking, coins

techniques.name: Dynasty-first anchoring
techniques.how: [Clue → dynasty] Before reading options, name the dynasty the stem's clue belongs to (title, era, text); then drop every option from another dynasty.
techniques.example: 'Gupta Era was started by' → era 319-20 = Chandragupta I's accession → Srigupta, Samudragupta, Kumaragupta fall → Chandragupta I [group1-prelims-2010-reexam#101]

techniques.name: Title-to-ruler lookup
techniques.how: Keep a fixed title table (Devanampiya, Siladitya, Kaviraja, Devaputra); a title question is then a lookup.
techniques.example: 'Devanam Priya' → Asoka; Kanishka = Devaputra, Samudragupta = Kaviraja, Harsha = Siladitya [group1-prelims-2008#112]

techniques.name: Odd-period elimination in multi-select
techniques.how: Date every listed item; the item outside the period is the one to drop, then choose the code that excludes only it.
techniques.example: Later Vedic pottery: BRW, BSW, PGW, Red Ware fit 1000-600 BC; NBPW is later → 'I, II, III and IV' [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#2]

techniques.name: Ruler sequence by succession chain
techniques.how: Write the father-son chain once (CG I - Samudra - CG II - Kumara I - Skanda) and match codes; only one code starts and ends correctly.
techniques.example: Only '(iii),(i),(iv),(ii)' starts with Samudragupta and ends with Skandagupta [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#14]

techniques.name: Site-to-signature find grid
techniques.how: Memorise one signature find per Indus site; reject options where the site's signature is a different find.
techniques.example: Bead industry → Chanhudaro; Dholavira = reservoirs, Daimabad = bronzes, Sutkagendor = coastal outpost [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#1]

techniques.name: Match grid by one sure pair
techniques.how: In matching, fix the pair you are surest of, strike codes that break it, then check one more pair.
techniques.example: Mahajanapadas: Anga-Champa alone leaves only 'A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV' [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#4]; Vaisheshika-atoms fixes the philosophy grid [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#3]

confusions.remember: Maurya = abdicated to Jainism; I = Gupta era 319; II = Sakari, Fa-Hien
Nanaghat = Naganika; Nasik = Gautami Balasri (Gautamiputra's mother)
Junagadh = first long Sanskrit inscription; Hathigumpha = Kalinga, Nanda canal
Aditi = mother of gods (Adityas); Prithvi = earth
Asura = purchase; Rakshasa = capture; Paisacha = seduction
Lokayata = materialism; Ajivika (Gosala) = niyati, fixed fate
Nagarjuna = Buddhist Sunyavada, Prajnaparamita; Kundakunda = Jain Samayasara
Gathasaptasati / Brihatkatha vs Katantra grammar / Lilavai
Hydaspes = Jhelum (Porus 326 BC); Hyphasis = Beas (where the army halted)
birth / enlightenment vs first sermon / death
PGW = Later Vedic; NBPW = Mahajanapada-Maurya (600-200 BC)
South = grahana-moksha, no annexation; West = Sakas annexed

anchors: Gupta era 319-20 AD from Chandragupta I; Saka era 78 AD; Vikrama 58 BC
Gupta order: Chandragupta I - Samudragupta - Chandragupta II - Kumaragupta I - Skandagupta
Purusha Sukta (Rigveda X.90) = first mention of four varnas
Satapatha Brahmana = first reference to moneylending (kusidin)
Hydaspes = Jhelum, Alexander vs Porus 326 BC
Asokan scripts: Brahmi, Kharosthi, Greek, Aramaic; name 'Asoka' in Maski and Gujarra; RE XIII names five Greek kings
Earliest inscriptions (Asoka's) = Prakrit in Brahmi script
Mahajanapada capitals: Avanti-Ujjain, Kosala-Shravasti, Vatsa-Kaushambi, Anga-Champa, Magadha-Rajagriha
IVC: Lothal dock and ivory scale; Chanhudaro beads; Kalibangan ploughed field; Mesopotamia = main trade partner (Meluhha)
Satavahanas = first dynasty to rule Andhra; inscriptions in Prakrit, Brahmi script
Sungas: Yavana invasion in Gargi Samhita, Mahabhashya, Malavikagnimitra
Kushans/Sakas introduced turban, trousers, long coat, helmet, boots
checklist: Which dynasty does the stem's clue belong to? Drop same-name rulers of other dynasties.
Is it a NOT / wrong-pair question? Mark the stem before reading options.
For 'which belong to period X', date every item; find the one outside the period.
For inscriptions and texts, recall issuer/author from a fixed table, not from familiarity.
In matching, lock the surest pair and strike codes.
For an absolute statement ('never', 'only'), test the fact itself before judging it.
